ut_secret_garden.blurb: Secret Garden is a bouldering area at the very bottom of Little Cottonwood Canyon, in Utah's Wasatch Range. Everything here is bouldering, spread over roughly fifteen boulders, with Copperhead Boulder holding the most climbs, followed by All Thumbs Boulder and Tiger Stripe Boulder. The grade range is wide. A warm-up boulder offers several easier problems, there is a solid block of moderates, and a thinner tail of hard problems runs well into the double-digit V grades, along with a number of open projects. The stone is described as high quality, and Copperhead is known for an overhanging face. Heat matters in summer, when climbers are steered to higher elevations in the canyon because the lowest boulders get too hot.

vt_bolton_dome.blurb: Bolton Dome is a south-facing cliff near Bolton in northern Vermont. Sport routes make up about half of the climbing, with a good share of trad and a couple of dozen boulder problems. Grades run from easy up to 5.13, with most of the roped climbs between 5.10 and 5.12, and the cliff is said to hold the highest concentration of 5.12- routes in Vermont. Walls such as Main Wall, Railroad Yard, West Side and Dometop each hold around a dozen climbs, while Green Up Boulder and Grandma's House cover much of the bouldering. Spring and fall are the recommended seasons. By June the cliff turns very hot, and in summer it is comfortable only on early mornings or cool days.

wa_north_cascades_core.blurb: North Cascades Core gathers high mountain objectives in and around North Cascades National Park in Washington, with Boston Basin and Eldorado Peak holding the most climbs. The climbing is mostly alpine routes and mountaineering, with a fair number of scrambles and a few ice lines. Grades sit mostly at class 3 and 4 terrain and moderate rock from 5.6 to 5.8. The park is described as wild and glaciated, with severe weather possible. In the wider North Cascades, summer is the time for alpine rock, the range holds most of the glaciers in the lower 48, and granite is mostly very good where it appears. At Eldorado Peak, in the Cascade River drainage, routes range from an easy walk with a knife-edge traverse up to WI3 ice, and the approach is long and strenuous.

wa_phun_rock_and_nearby_crags.blurb: Phun Rock and its nearby crags form a cluster of sport walls west of Mazama, in Washington's Okanogan. Nearly every route is bolted. Grades start around 5.5 and reach 5.13, with most between 5.9 and 5.12 and 5.10 and 5.11 the most common. The area mixes family-friendly moderates with some tougher lines. The holds are described as positive, difficulty rises with steepness, and the popular routes are now clean and solid, though less-used sections can be dirty and loose. K-9 Crag holds the most climbs, followed by A-Wall, Rhinozone and Romance Rock, with Squirrelhouse Rock, Sun Rock and Ripple Rock adding smaller walls. Across Mazama as a whole, sport climbing is the main style.

_expect.name: Area 5: Red and White Grotto Walls

wy_area_5_red_and_white_grotto_walls.blurb: Area 5, the Red and White Grotto Walls, is a group of red walls in Guernsey State Park, Wyoming, on the North Platte River. The climbing is almost entirely bolted sport, mostly 5.10 and 5.11 with a handful of easier lines and some at 5.12. Red Clove Wall holds the most climbs, followed by Hot Cinnamon Wall, Switchbax Power Tower Wall and Maroon Towers Wall. The red rock is iron-stained orthoquartzite capped by gray dolomite, with only intermittent cracks, so the climbing leans on palm holds, pockets, steep walls and roofs. Rock quality is highly varied and unpredictable, and much of the park's climbing is on fractured stone. Across the park, some south-facing walls are often among the warmest winter climbing in Wyoming.

ab_the_lookout.blurb: The Lookout is a sport climbing area in Echo Canyon, in Alberta's Bow Valley. Every route is bolted, and the grades lean hard: 5.12 and 5.13 make up most of the climbs, with a smaller group of 5.11s and a few easier lines. Atlantis Wall holds the most climbs, followed by the main wall and its shield, The Cave, Bellavista and The Balcony. Echo Canyon's routes are described as techy, pumpy and crimpy, on stone of consistent quality. The Lookout gets plenty of sun and is not a summer crag; the lower part of the main wall has almost no shade and runs hot and exposed. Fall is named as the best time in the canyon, and early and late season suit the Lookout itself.
